import os
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import log_loss
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

INPUT_DIR = "./input"
SUBMISSION_DIR = "./submission"
TRAIN_FILE = os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, "train.csv")
TEST_FILE = os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, "test.csv")
SAMPLE_SUBMISSION = os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, "sample_submission.csv")
SUBMISSION_PATH = os.path.join(SUBMISSION_DIR, "submission.csv")

os.makedirs(SUBMISSION_DIR, exist_ok=True)

# Load sample submission to get exact column names
spec_columns = []
if os.path.exists(SAMPLE_SUBMISSION):
    spec_df = pd.read_csv(SAMPLE_SUBMISSION)
    species_cols = [col for col in spec_df.columns if col != "id"]
else:
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"Sample submission not found at {SAMPLE_SUBMISSION}")

print(f"Number of species classes: {len(species_cols)}")

# Load training data
train_df = pd.read_csv(TRAIN_FILE)
feature_column_list = [col for col in train_df.columns if col not in ["id", "species"]]
print(f"Features identified: {len(feature_column_list)}")

X_train_raw = train_df[feature_column_list].values
y_train = train_df["species"].values

# Map species labels to integers (consistent order for predict_proba output)
label_map = {}
reverse_label_map = {}
unique_classes = np.unique(y_train)
n_classes = len(unique_classes)
for i, species in enumerate(unique_classes):
    label_map[species] = i
    reverse_label_map[i] = species

y_train_mapped = np.array([label_map[s] for s in y_train])

# CRITICAL FIX: Split into strict train + held-out validation sets BEFORE any processing
# Use stratified split to maintain class distribution
X_train_set, X_val, y_train_mapped, y_val = train_test_split(
    X_train_raw, y_train_mapped, test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=y_train_mapped
)

# CRITICAL FIX: Scale ONLY on the training set, not including validation
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train_set)
X_val_scaled = scaler.transform(X_val)

# Ensure species_cols order matches the label_map order (predict_proba output order)
# Create mapping from column index in submition header to label index in model
submission_species_idx_map = {
    species_name: i for i, species_name in enumerate(species_cols)
}

# Train model on training set ONLY (REMOVED LEAGIC REGRESSION FOR ENSEMBLE IMPROVEMENT)
model = RandomForestClassifier(
    n_estimators=200,
    max_depth=10,
    min_samples_split=5,
    min_samples_leaf=2,
    n_jobs=-1,
    random_state=42,
    class_weight="balanced",
)
model.fit(X_train_scaled, y_train_mapped)

# Validate on TRUE HIDDEN VALIDATION SET (never seen during training or scaling)
val_preds_proba = model.predict_proba(X_val_scaled)
val_logloss = log_loss(y_val, val_preds_proba)
print(f"Held-out Validation Log Loss: {val_logloss:.6f}")

# Prepare test data for submission
test_df = pd.read_csv(TEST_FILE)
# Feature names in test should match training features
# Extract feature columns from test file (should match X_train features)
X_test_raw = test_df[feature_column_list].values
# IMPORTANT: Apply the SAME scaler trained on training set to test data
X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test_raw)

# Generate predictions on test set
test_preds_proba = model.predict_proba(X_test_scaled)

# CRITICAL FIX: Build submission dataframe aligned with sample_submission format
# Test df row order must correspond to submission order
submission_probs = np.zeros((len(test_df), len(species_cols)))

# Align prediction columns with species_cols order
# Model predict_proba returns classes in the order they appear during fit
# We need to match these indices back to species string names in submission header
for col_idx in range(len(species_cols)):
    species_name = species_cols[col_idx]
    int_label_idx = label_map[species_name]
    # Assign probabilities from model output at this integer label index
    submission_probs[:, col_idx] = test_preds_proba[:, int_label_idx]

# Clamping probabilities to avoid extreme values before submission
submission_probs_clamped = np.clip(submission_probs, 1e-15, 1 - 1e-15)

# Create final submission dataframe
test_ids = test_df["id"].values
submission_data = np.column_stack([test_ids, submission_probs_clamped])
submission_df = pd.DataFrame(submission_data, columns=["id"] + species_cols)

# Save submission file at REQUIRED LOCATION
submission_df.to_csv(SUBMISSION_PATH, index=False)
print(f"Submission saved to: {SUBMISSION_PATH}")
print(f"Total predictions: {len(submission_df)}")

# Final summary
print(f"\n=== Final Results ===")
print(f"Held-out Validation Log Loss: {val_logloss:.6f}")
print(f"Best Held-out Validation Score achieved:")
